subject: Ganondorf
text: Reflecting Ganondorf's energy balls back at him stuns him, after which shooting him with a Light Arrow stuns him further for Link to attack.

evidence.quote:
Ganondorf will reflect the balls back at you as well, so keeping reflecting
them until one strikes and stuns Ganondorf.  There is a new wrinkle to the
fight at this point; you must now shoot Ganondorf with a Light Arrow, whereupon
he will become stunned.

subject: Ganondorf
text: Link can equip Hover Boots to cross the central pit and perform a Jump Attack while crossing to hit the stunned Ganondorf.

evidence.quote:
Quickly equip the Hover Boots and use them to cross the pit in the middle of
the floor.  Just like in the Twinrova fight, use a Jump Attack when you're
halfway across the pit to deal extra damage to him, then switch to normal
attacks.

subject: Ganondorf
text: When Ganondorf charges up power with both arms raised, shooting him with a Light Arrow cancels the attack and stuns him instantly.

evidence.quote:
Ganondorf will occasionally use a new attack where he will charge up a lot of
power (you'll know when he's doing it, as he will hold up both arms to create
the spell instead of just one arm for the Lightning Ball).  To stop him from
using this attack, shoot him with a Light Arrow.  This will instantly stun him,
letting you get in more attacks.

subject: Ganon
text: Ganon's weak point is his tail, which can be reached during the first phase by Z-Targeting him and performing side dodges.

evidence.quote:
Like all evil demons of the underworld, Ganon's weakspot is his tail.  In his
first phase, you'll have to Z-Target Ganon and then begin performing side
dodges (hold right or left and press A) to speed around behind Ganon.

subject: Ganon
text: In the first phase of the Ganon fight without the Master Sword, Link can deal heavy damage to Ganon's tail using Jump Attacks with the Biggoron Sword or Megaton Hammer.

evidence.quote:
At the start of the fight you won't have access to the Master Sword.  Which
doesn't really matter, since Shields are useless against Ganon, and you should
have the Biggoron Sword by now.  If for whatever reason you don't have the
Biggoron Sword, then the Megaton Hammer will have to make due...When you
get behind him, do a Jump Attack with the Biggoron Sword or Megaton Hammer to
deal a hefty amount of damage to Ganon.

subject: Master Sword
text: When the surrounding ring of fire lowers during the Ganon battle, Link must run to Zelda to retrieve the Master Sword.

evidence.quote:
Repeat this method until a cutscene shows the flames around the perimeter of
the arena lowering.  Run over to Zelda and retake the Master Sword when this
happens.

subject: Ganon
text: Ganon can only be finished off with the Master Sword while held in place by Princess Zelda's magic.

evidence.quote:
Only the Master Sword can defeat Ganon.  After a
cutscene, you will be prompted to attack Ganondorf while he is being held in
place by Zelda's magic.  Do this, and the game is over.

subject: Mido
text: Mido will not let Link pass to the Great Deku Tree unless both the Kokiri Sword and Deku Shield are equipped in the Equipment subscreen.

evidence.quote:
Make sure you have them equipped in the Equipment subscreen.  If either the
Kokiri Sword or the Deku Shield is not equipped, then Mido will not let you
pass.

subject: Game File Number
text: The number displayed on the game file tracks how many times the player has reached the Game Over screen on that file, excluding deaths revived with a Fairy.

evidence.quote:
The real
answer is, this number records the number of times you have seen the Game Over
screen on that file (deaths that were recovered with a Fairy don't count).

subject: Deku Nut Upgrade
text: The Deku Nut upgrade from the Forest Stage cannot be obtained once Link has transformed into Adult Link.

evidence.quote:
Q: Why can't I get the Deku Nut Upgrade from the Forest Stage?

A: This upgrade cannot be gotten if you have already become Adult Link.

subject: Triforce
text: When young Link opens the Door of Time, the Sacred Realm is unsealed and the three Triforce pieces go to Ganondorf (Power), Link (Courage), and Zelda (Wisdom).

evidence.quote:
When Link opens the Door
of Time in his childhood, then the Sacred Realm was unsealed.  The three shards
of the Triforce (Power, Courage and Wisdom) each went to a different person in
the world: Ganondorf got the Triforce of Power, Link got the Triforce of
Courage, and Zelda got the Triforce of Wisdom.

subject: Zora's Domain
text: Zora's Domain cannot be manually thawed out during gameplay, but begins unfreezing after beating the Water Temple and is shown unfrozen during the credits.

evidence.quote:
Q: How do I unfreeze Zora's Domain?

A: Short answer: you can't.

Long answer: Zora's Domain begins to unfreeze after you beat the Water Temple...Zora's Domain unfreezes eventually.  We know this, as
Zoras appear in the party at Lon Lon Ranch during the credits.

subject: Gold Skulltula
text: Dropping a Bottled Bug into soft earth patches as Young Link reveals a Gold Skulltula in nine locations across Hyrule.

evidence.quote:
As Young Link, travel to the patches of
soft earth (Kokiri Forest, Lake Hylia, Gerudo Valley, Death Mountain Trail,
Death Mountain Crater, Kakariko Graveyard, Desert Colossus, and two in the Lost
Woods) and drop a Bottled Bug into the patch.  Each of the patches will produce
a Gold Skulltula.

subject: Zora's River Soft Earth
text: The soft earth patch located at Zora's River does not contain a Gold Skulltula.

evidence.quote:
For whatever reason, the patch of soft earth at Zora's River
does not contain a Gold Skulltula.

subject: Skull Kid
text: The Skull Kid in the Lost Woods will only buy the Skull Mask if Link has already played Saria's Song for him and earned the Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote:
Q: How come I can't sell the Skull Mask to the Skullkid?

A: He will only buy the mask from you if you've already played him Saria's Song
and earned the Piece of Heart.

subject: Kakariko Village Windmill
text: Link can use the Longshot to access hidden openings inside the Kakariko Village Windmill, but they serve no purpose.

evidence.quote:
you can use the Longshot
to access hidden openings in the Kakariko Village Windmill.  These openings do
nothing.

subject: East Lava Pit
text: Crossing the lava pit on the east side of Goron City requires playing the Song of Time to summon a Block of Time, then using the Longshot to pull across to Business Scrubs.

evidence.quote:
You need both the Longshot and the Song of Time to get across the pit.  Play
the Song of Time to make a Block of Time appear, then stand on the block to use
the Longshot and pull yourself across the lava pit.  What's on the other side?
A pit containing Business Scrubs, selling rubbish.

subject: Gerudo Valley Rupee Arrow
text: The arrow formed of rupees in the pit in Gerudo Valley points only to a plain wall with nothing behind it.

evidence.quote:
Q: What does the arrow made of rupees point to in the pit in Gerudo Valley?

A: The wall.  There is nothing there.

subject: Running Man
text: As Adult Link, Link can challenge the Running Man to a footrace time trial from the Gerudo Valley Carpenter's Tent to the entrance to Kokiri Forest, though the Running Man always finishes one second faster.

evidence.quote:
As Adult Link, you can challenge the Running Man who bought your Bunny Hood
as a child to a footrace from the Gerudo Valley Carpenter's Tent to the
entrance to Kokiri Forest.  It doesn't matter how fast you go, he'll always
beat you by exactly one second...In the end, it seems that all the Running Man is a time trial to see how
quickly you can travel from Gerudo Valley to Kokiri Forest.  He does, after
all, keep track of your best time.

subject: Gold Skulltula Trick
text: In the Hyrule Castle Garden pit opened with Song of Storms, Link can kill the Gold Skulltula, retrieve its token with the Boomerang, and backflip into the exit light before the token touches him to collect unlimited tokens.

evidence.quote:
This trick lets you get unlimited Gold Skulltula tokens, even past the 100
mark (the Quest Subscreen even shows the number going above 100).  To perform
this trick, head for the pit in Hyrule Castle Garden which can only be opened
with the Song of Storms.  It's near the tree in the area with Talon's Milk
Crates.  Drop down into the pit, and look for the Gold Skulltula.  Kill it, and
then Z-Target its token.  Use the Boomerang on the token, and then backflip
into the beam of light leading back to the surface just before the Token
touches you.
